subject: A challenge cannot say its box is REAL, so a real-box challenge renders a dead Launch Box link
description: Hit live 2026-09-22 on Engine 1 Live Fire. tournament-board.html:831 renders a 'Launch Box' button whenever a challenge has a boxId, linking to /arena/boxes/<boxId>/index.html. That field means 'this challenge has a SIMULATED arena box'. A challenge backed by a REAL machine has no arena box, so any boxId value produces a 404 (confirmed: /arena/boxes/engine1/index.html returns HTTP 404 and no such directory exists), and the student sees two routes to the machine, one of which is broken. The only way to suppress it today is to OMIT boxId entirely, which is what was done. That works but it is implicit: nothing tells the next person wiring a real box that setting boxId will render a dead link, and nothing in the console warns when a challenge has both a boxId and a real-box assignment. Worse, boxId is load-bearing elsewhere - deliverFlag's guard (functions/index.js:774) uses it to withhold flags for boxes in use as tournament challenges - so 'just omit it' is correct for a real box and WRONG for a simulated one, and the difference is invisible. Remedy options: an explicit flag on the challenge (realBox: true) that suppresses the Launch Box link; or render the link only when the boxId resolves to a box that exists in box-catalog.json; or have the console refuse to save a challenge that carries both a boxId and a pool assignment. The second is the most self-correcting because it cannot drift from the catalog.
